purpose: Describe the important pages, user interactions, and journeys for the handmade-goods store. This is a behavioral reference, not a prescribed UI layout or technical implementation.

global_experience.store_identity: The store should feel personal, trustworthy, and focused on the craft behind handmade products.
expectations: Shoppers can understand where they are and what they can do next.
The cart count and cart contents remain consistent throughout the shopping journey.
Errors explain what went wrong and how to recover.
The experience works across mobile, tablet, and desktop.

subfooter: Accepted payment methods (text labels, marked as demo)

pages.purpose: Introduce the store and encourage shoppers to discover its products.
content: A concise introduction to the handmade products
An inviting visual introduction to the products or craftsmanship
A clear path to browse the catalog
A row of four reassurances just above the footer: named makers, returns, shipping, contact (CR-005)
success_criteria: A first-time visitor can understand what the store sells.
The path from the home page to the catalog is obvious.

pages.purpose: Help shoppers discover and compare products.
content: Product imagery, names, prices, and brief descriptions
Product categories or other useful discovery aids where appropriate
interactions: Open a product to see its details.
Filter products if filtering is supported.
Clear an active filter to see the full collection.
states: Unavailable catalog or error, if applicable
success_criteria: Shoppers can identify products and understand their basic differences.
Selecting a product opens the correct product details.

pages.purpose: Help shoppers understand a product and configure it before purchasing.
interactions: See price changes resulting from selected options.
Add a valid configuration to the cart.
success_criteria: Shoppers understand what they will receive and how much it costs.
Required choices are clear before purchase.
Invalid or unavailable configurations cannot be added to the cart.
After adding an item, shoppers receive clear feedback and can continue shopping or view the cart.

pages.purpose: Let shoppers review and modify their intended purchase.
content: Quantities, unit prices, and line totals
Cart subtotal and any clearly labeled demo charges
interactions: Proceed to checkout when the cart contains items.
success_criteria: Shoppers can identify exactly what they intend to purchase.
Changes to the cart update its contents, item count, and totals consistently.
An empty cart provides a clear path back to shopping.

pages.purpose: Collect the information needed to demonstrate a completed order.
content: An explicit notice that checkout is simulated
success_criteria: Required information is validated with understandable messages.
Entered information is preserved when validation fails.
The order summary agrees with the cart.
No payment-card information is requested or collected.
Successful submission leads to an order confirmation.

pages.purpose: Confirm that the demo order was created and summarize the purchase.
content: Purchased products, configurations, quantities, and totals
A clear indication that this is a demo order
success_criteria: The confirmation matches the submitted order.
Refreshing the confirmation does not create a duplicate order.
An unknown order reference produces a helpful recovery path.

pages.purpose: Explain returns, exchanges and refunds so shoppers can buy with confidence.
content: Summary of the policy at a glance
A route to contact the studio
success_criteria: A shopper can find the return window and refund timing within a few seconds.
Final-sale rules for personalized items are unambiguous.

pages.purpose: Answer common shopper questions without contacting the studio.
content: Questions grouped by topic: orders and shipping, returns, personalization, care, this demo
A route to contact the studio
success_criteria: Answers are keyboard accessible and readable on mobile.

pages.purpose: Show shoppers how to reach the studio.
content: Notice that this is a demo store and messages are not monitored
success_criteria: Contact details are easy to copy.
No form submits or transmits data.

primary_journeys.name: Discover a product and complete a purchase
steps: Review its details and select any required options.
Add the configured product to the cart.
Enter valid contact and shipping information.
primary_journeys.expected_outcome: The shopper reaches a confirmation that accurately reflects the selected products and agreed totals.

primary_journeys.name: Recover from an invalid product selection
steps: Open a product with required options.
Leave a required option unselected or select an unavailable configuration.
Attempt to add the product to the cart.
Receive clear guidance about the issue.
primary_journeys.expected_outcome: No invalid configuration enters the cart, and the shopper can recover without losing unrelated choices.

primary_journeys.name: Modify a cart before checkout
primary_journeys.expected_outcome: The cart contents, item count, and totals consistently reflect the latest changes.

design_intent.note: Added after the first build. The original specs left overall style to the builder, which is a gap: this is something the owner should choose during onboarding.

style.direction: not chosen by the owner. The builder used a warm, contemporary craft look.

design_principles: Product imagery and craftsmanship should be prominent.
Browsing pages use the full screen width; product cards give the image most of the space (CR-003, CR-004).
Visual styling should feel cohesive, considered, and appropriate for an independent handmade-goods brand.
The interface should make available actions and current state understandable.
Primary actions should be easy to identify without overwhelming the page.
Layouts should adapt naturally to different screen sizes.
Accessibility, readable contrast, keyboard operation, and meaningful form labels are expected.
The implementation agent may choose the visual design and interaction details that best fulfill these goals.

implementation_guidance.instruction: Choose page layouts, components, routes, state management, and interaction patterns based on good product and engineering judgment. The page descriptions and journeys define expected user-facing behavior, not a mandatory implementation. Document significant assumptions or deviations.
